messages:
maria: heads-up — saw recurring throughput oscillations on the p99 path during the last canary. looks correlated with kernel handoffs when KV hit-rate bounces between 60-90%. logs attached below. :frowning:

maria: snippet from the profiler:
```
[2026-03-18T15:02:12Z] batch_assemble: wait 12ms
[2026-03-18T15:02:12Z] kv_check: hit 78%
[2026-03-18T15:02:12Z] kernel_select: switch from int8-qkv -> fp16-opt (20us)
[2026-03-18T15:02:12Z] kernel_warmup: compile 3ms
```

dan: that compile/warmup during handoff is the killer. when KV drops we prefer a faster kernel but the runtime reconfigs and we pay the penalty.

kevin: can we debounce kernel selection? e.g., require X consecutive batches before switching, or smooth by token-weighted moving average of hit-rate.

maria: yes — had a quick experiment with EMA on KV-hit and a 3-batch hysteresis. reduced oscillation but increased tail latency on cold-starts.

sophie: tradeoff is obvious. maybe separate policies: aggressive on steady-state requests, conservative during ramp-ups. also consider admitting slightly smaller batches until kernel is stable.

kevin: proposal: two knobs — hit_rate_ema_alpha and kernel_hold_batches. default alpha=0.3, hold=4. and if hold_active then force kernel-stick. also add an admit-smoothing window that prevents immediate up/down admit decisions for token_budget for 200ms.

maria: +1. we should also tweak soft-429 emission: if kernel switch probability > 0.2 and queue depth > threshold then emit soft-429 to downstream clients to avoid cascading stalls.

dan: how would soft-429 be scored? single header or body hint? we should include a backoff-suggestion header + metric tag for tracing. e.g., `X-Redwood-Backoff: soft-429; retry_after=150`

kevin: implementation sketch in config form:
```yaml
runtime:
  kernel_selection:
    hit_rate_ema_alpha: 0.25
    hold_batches: 4
    min_stable_tokens: 64
  admit_control:
    token_budget_window_ms: 200
    min_lease_ms: 50
    soft_429_policy:
      enabled: true
      switch_prob_threshold: 0.2
      queue_depth_threshold: 80
      retry_header: "X-Redwood-Backoff"
```

sophie: note: min_stable_tokens is important for tiny requests (short sequences) — otherwise we flicker kernels on any short prompt.

maria: perf experiment plan: A/B two cohorts on canary fleet for 6h each. measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, kernel_switch_count, kv_hit_ema, soft_429_rate. we want switch_count down >=50% and no regression on p99 > 5%.

infra-bot: deploy candidate/osc-damp-v1 to canary fleet (tag: osc-damp-2026-03-18) — started at 2026-03-18T15:20:00Z.

dan: add dashboards: kernel_switches per minute, kv_hit_ema (per model), soft_429_rate, upstream_retries. alert if soft_429_rate > 3% for >10m.

kevin: quick perf note — we should also sample kernel warmup cost separately: measure compile_time and first_batch_penalty. if compile_time > 5ms we should prefer cached compiled kernels or skip switch.

maria: action items:
- kevin: implement hit_rate_ema + hold_batches, add metrics (kernel_switch_count, hold_active).
- dan: dashboard + soft_429 tracing header work.
- sophie: run A/B plan and collect perf traces.
- maria: run short simulation to tune alpha/hold before deploy.

kevin: taking kevin. aiming PR today for config + tests.

sophie: targing data collection tomorrow morning, will drop a summary in this thread. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks — appreciate the quick turn. we'll keep the policy conservative initially and relax as we confirm stability. :thumbsup:
